row.subject: h-raticate.txt: the 12 cards other than Team Rocket's Raticate ex (Alolan Vulpix, Alolan Ninetales ex, Team Rocket's Rattata, Professor's Research, Copycat, Cyrus, Sabrina, Poké Ball, Repel, Elegant Cape, Soothing Shore, Training Area)
row.card_text:
Texts come from lib/card.py and match the engine database word for word.
- Alolan Vulpix A3 040: Water Basic, 60 HP, weak Metal, retreat 1. [W] Call Forth Cold, 0 damage: "Take a [W] Energy from your Energy Zone and attach it to this Pokémon."
- Alolan Ninetales ex B2 029: Water Stage 1 from Alolan Vulpix, 150 HP, weak Metal, retreat 2. [WW] Binding Snow 80: "During your opponent's next turn, they can't take any Energy from their Energy Zone to attach to their Active Pokémon."

- Copycat B1 225 (Supporter): "Shuffle your hand into your deck. Draw a card for each card in your opponent's hand."

findings.clause: Alolan Vulpix: 60 HP, Water, Basic, weak Metal, retreat 1, worth 1 point
findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values. Knockout points come from the name: no 'ex' and no 'Mega' means 1 point.
findings.evidence: engine/src/database.rs 18921-18944; models/card.rs 186-216. Card.py matches. S38 (010207) shows the card in play. The Gemini-only claim that Vulpix retreated for 0 Energy (open_questions #4) was never confirmed on footage, and the card says 1.

findings.clause: Call Forth Cold: [W] cost, 0 damage; take a [W] from the Energy Zone and attach it to this Pokémon. Mandatory, no choice.
findings.engine_does: Maps to SelfChargeActive{[Water]} and calls attach_energy_from_zone(actor, 0, Water, 1, is_turn_energy=false). This creates a new Water Energy on the attacking Active. It does not use up the turn's Energy, and it is Water whatever the deck's types. No player choice. It needs [W], so the player going first cannot use it on turn 1.
findings.evidence: actions/effect_mechanic_map.rs 1852-1857; apply_attack_action.rs 389-391 and 2700-2710; state/energy.rs 13-33. No engine test names this attack, and no recording shows it (claims.json and second_pass have zero hits).

findings.clause: Call Forth Cold under an opposing Binding Snow
findings.engine_does: attach_energy_from_zone refuses to attach to slot 0 while NoEnergyFromZoneToActive is active, so the attack does 0 damage and adds nothing. That is right, because Binding Snow says 'any Energy from their Energy Zone'.
findings.evidence: state/energy.rs 21-23 and 76-85. There is no Ninetales in the panel, so this never comes up in table games.

findings.clause: Alolan Ninetales ex: 150 HP, Water, Stage 1 from 'Alolan Vulpix', weak Metal, retreat 2, ex worth 2 points
findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values. It evolves only from the name 'Alolan Vulpix'. The last word 'ex' gives 2 points.
findings.evidence: database.rs 54181-54201; models/card.rs 186-216.

findings.clause: Binding Snow: [WW], 80 damage
findings.engine_does: Deals 80 through active_damage_effect_doutcome, then applies the lock. Training Area makes it 90, because the attacker is Stage 1.
findings.evidence: effect_mechanic_map.rs 586-592; apply_attack_action.rs 719-721 and 3456-3465; hooks/core.rs 1817-1832.

findings.clause: Binding Snow lock: how long it lasts ('during your opponent's next turn')
findings.engine_does: add_turn_effect(effect, 1) stores the lock for turn_count N and N+1. It is keyed by turn number, so it runs out after the opponent's next turn. Being stored for turn N, the attacker's own turn, has no effect: the attack ends that turn. After the attack, the only zone attachment to one's own Active the engine knows is Zeraora's, on turns 1-2, and Binding Snow cannot be used that early.
findings.evidence: state/mod.rs 1063-1086; hooks/core.rs 521-552.

findings.clause: Binding Snow lock: what it blocks (Energy Zone to the Active only; Bench still allowed; Energy from other sources still allowed)
findings.engine_does: can_attach_energy_from_zone returns false only for in_play_idx 0. It is checked when offering the turn's Energy (Bench slots are still offered), inside attach_energy_from_zone (which covers every zone attachment: turn Energy, Abilities, attack self-charges), and before offering Ice Maker (Baxcalibur, Suicune deck). Discard-pile attachments are not blocked (Flame Patch, via attach_energy_from_discard), and the text doesn't block them either. Nightmare Aura (Darkrai ex, Weezing deck) cannot trigger on a blocked attachment, because the trigger runs only after a successful attachment.
findings.evidence: move_generation/mod.rs 76-92; state/energy.rs 13-33, 53-85, 117-170; move_generation_abilities.rs 361-371. rules/_research_notes/audit_2026-09-22/attacks1.md:97 'A75 DamageAndTurnEffect/NoEnergyFromZoneToActive: OK'. No engine test and no recording of Binding Snow.

findings.clause: Binding Snow lock: whose Active counts (ambiguous in Pocket: a player-wide lock, or tied to the Pokémon hit)
findings.engine_does: Treats it as a lock on the player. It keeps applying if Ninetales is knocked out or leaves the Active Spot, and it blocks whichever Pokémon is Active at the moment of attaching, including one promoted, switched in or retreated to. That follows the wording ('they ... their Active Pokémon'), which targets the player, not 'the Defending Pokémon'. So the Pocket rule that attack effects end when a Pokémon goes to the Bench does not obviously apply.
findings.evidence: The turn effect is keyed by turn number, not by a Pokémon: state/mod.rs 1063-1086; state/energy.rs 76-85. No recording confirms or contradicts this.

findings.clause: Binding Snow side effect on an opponent's Roar in Unison (Hydreigon B1 157, Hydreigon panel deck)
findings.engine_does: Roar in Unison's move generation checks only ability_used, not the lock. So an Active Hydreigon under the lock is offered the Ability. Using it attaches nothing and does no self-damage (the 30 applies only 'if attached'), but it uses up the once-per-turn Ability. That is a no-op option Pocket would probably not offer. Ice Maker is checked correctly. This does not make Binding Snow stronger than its text. At most it lets a careless pilot waste an Ability.
findings.evidence: move_generation_abilities.rs 120 (no lock check) compared with 366 (Ice Maker checks it); apply_abilities_action.rs 695-716.

findings.clause: Team Rocket's Rattata: 40 HP, Colorless, Basic, weak Fighting, retreat 1, worth 1 point
findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values.
findings.evidence: database.rs 80428-80449. Recording S199 shows HP 40. S86 (a retreat for 0) was 'cannot_determine' and inferred only.

findings.clause: Ambush: [C] 20; one coin; heads +20; no other effect
findings.engine_does: CoinFlipExtraDamage{20} gives a 50/50 split between 40 and 20. Training Area adds nothing, because Rattata is a Basic.
findings.evidence: effect_mechanic_map.rs 1013-1016; apply_attack_action.rs 581-583 and 1891-1896. Recordings S115 (40 on heads, twice) and S105 (tails 20, cut to 0 by Coordinated Unit), both engine_matches.

findings.clause: Professor's Research: Supporter, draw 2
findings.engine_does: Discarded before its effect, sets has_played_support, then calls maybe_draw_card twice. Draws stop at the 10-card hand limit. It cannot be played with an empty deck, as rules/04 says.
findings.evidence: apply_trainer_action.rs 103-105 and 1850-1855; move_generation_trainer.rs 550-559; apply_action_helpers.rs 971-996; state/mod.rs 811-831. Recordings R155 and S22 match. Test: engine/tests/s187_f017_professors_research.rs.

findings.clause: Copycat: Supporter; shuffle your whole hand into the deck; draw one card per card in the opponent's hand
findings.engine_does: Copycat is discarded first. The opponent's hand size is read before the shuffle, the remaining hand goes into the deck and is shuffled, then that many cards are drawn (up to 10 in hand). It has no empty-deck block, which rules/04 marks as the exception. It can still be played when the opponent has 0 cards; the Altaria check lists that case as open and ambiguous.
findings.evidence: apply_trainer_action.rs 2176-2197; move_generation_trainer.rs 239; apply_action_helpers.rs 990-991. Recordings R142, R143, S15, S16 match. Test: s189_hidden_zone_eligibility.rs 150-178.

findings.clause: Cyrus: Supporter; the user chooses 1 of the opponent's DAMAGED Benched Pokémon and switches it into the Active Spot
findings.engine_does: Only offered when at least one opposing Benched Pokémon is damaged. The actor chooses among the damaged ones. The switch is free, and the Pokémon moved to the Bench loses its conditions and attack effects.
findings.evidence: move_generation_trainer.rs 636-648; apply_trainer_action.rs 146-148 and 871-885; apply_action.rs 823-830; apply_action_helpers.rs 939-966. Recordings R100 and S66 match, and rules/04 §3 agrees.

findings.clause: Sabrina: Supporter; switch out the opponent's Active; the OPPONENT chooses the new Active
findings.engine_does: Only offered when the opponent has a Bench. The choice goes on the opponent's stack. The switch is free and clears the conditions of the Pokémon sent to the Bench.
findings.evidence: move_generation_trainer.rs 625-634; apply_trainer_action.rs 138-141 and 841-854. Recordings R102 (three battles), R162 and S66 match. rules/04 §3 records Sabrina seen four times.

findings.clause: Poké Ball: Item; put a random Basic Pokémon from your deck into your hand (random, no choice, hidden)
findings.engine_does: Each Basic copy in the deck is equally likely. The card goes to the hand, then the deck is shuffled. If no Basic is left, nothing is found but the card is still used. It can't be played with an empty deck. The opponent does not see the result. Per copy vs per name is open in Pocket (rules/05 #24); the engine uses per copy, which fits the wording 'a random Basic Pokémon'.
findings.evidence: apply_trainer_action.rs 99-101; shared_mutations.rs 16-28 and 137-175; move_generation_trainer.rs 561-570. Recordings R148, R153, S12, S13 and S14 match. R154's 'revealed to both' was refuted by the skeptics.

findings.clause: Repel: Item; the opponent's Active must be a BASIC; switch it out; the OPPONENT chooses
findings.engine_does: Offered only if the top card of the opponent's Active is a stage-0 Pokémon card and they have a Bench. The choice goes to the opponent. One small gap: a Fossil in play is 'a 40-HP Basic [C] Pokémon' (Helix Fossil text), but Card::is_basic() is false for Trainer-type Fossils, so Repel can't target one. That makes Repel weaker, not stronger, and no panel deck has Fossils.
findings.evidence: move_generation_trainer.rs 650-661; apply_trainer_action.rs 156 and 856-869; models/card.rs 243-248 (hooks/core.rs 105-117 does treat Fossils as Basic). No recording shows Repel, and no engine test names it.

findings.clause: Elegant Cape: Tool; +30 HP only while the holder is Stage 1; one Tool per Pokémon; attachable to any Pokémon
findings.engine_does: Can be attached to any of your own Pokémon without a Tool. The +30 is worked out each time HP is read, and only while the top card is stage 1. It stays attached through evolution, so a Cape on Rattata starts counting when it becomes Raticate ex (150 HP), and Ninetales ex with a Cape has 180. Removing it (Field Blower) drops HP at once.
findings.evidence: tools.rs 119-133; state/played_card.rs 289-310; apply_action.rs 1503-1528. Recordings R109 and S48, correction #1 (023151), and rules/02:131 (Type: Null 80 with a Cape, then Silvally 140, seen twice). Tests: tool_effect_gating_test.rs 24-33, tools_integration_test.rs 82-85.

findings.clause: Soothing Shore: Stadium; at the end of each player's turn, THAT player heals 20 from each of their Pokémon (Active and Bench) with any [W] attached
findings.engine_does: on_end_turn(player_ending_turn) heals 20 on each of that player's Pokémon holding at least one Water, Bench included. It happens after the attack and its knockouts and before the Pokémon Checkup, and Heal Block stops it. Water taken from a Water opponent counts, which fits 'any [W] Energy'. It can't be played while a Stadium with the same name is in play, which matters because the Suicune panel deck also plays it.
findings.evidence: hooks/core.rs 569 and 605-616; state/mod.rs 877-891; move_generation_trainer.rs 399-428. Recordings R91, R231, S55 and S187 (heal before the Checkup) match. Tests: soothing_shore_test.rs 24-115.

findings.clause: Training Area: Stadium; +10 for attacks by Stage 1 attackers on either side; to the opponent's Active only; before Weakness
findings.engine_does: Adds 10 when the attacker's top card is stage 1 and the attack is Active to Active. Nothing is added on Bench hits, and nothing for Basics or Stage 2s. The bonus goes in before Weakness. Raticate ex's Boost Dash does 80 and Binding Snow 90. The opponents' Stage 1s get the same +10 (Mega Lucario ex, Mega Altaria ex, Espeon, Vespiquen ex, Team Rocket's Weezing ex). A 0-damage attack gets no bonus.
findings.evidence: stadiums.rs 129-137; hooks/core.rs 105-117, 1817-1832 and 1854-1861. Recordings R108, S37, S40, S108, S110 and S111 match. Tests: stadium_test.rs 324-476 and 683-727.

findings.clause: Stadium play rules shared by Soothing Shore and Training Area (one per turn, replaces the one in play, same name blocked)
findings.engine_does: has_played_stadium limits Stadiums to one per turn. A Stadium with the same name as the one in play is blocked. A new one replaces yours or the opponent's, and the old card goes to its owner's discard.
findings.evidence: move_generation_trainer.rs 399-428; apply_action_helpers.rs 977-987. Recording R88 and RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md match.

row.impact_if_wrong:
None of these 12 cards gives the Raticate list more than its card text allows. They are unlikely to explain the +16 kp3 excess, and they cannot explain it under k3: every one of them works the same for both pilots, and k3 already matches Limitless (41.1 against 41.2).

The one card here whose value a pilot could change is Binding Snow. k3 leaves its lock unpriced, because the lock pays off on the opponent's turn. The lock is implemented exactly as written: it blocks Energy Zone attachments to the Active for one opponent turn, and the Bench and discard-pile attachments stay open.

If Pocket actually ends the lock when Ninetales leaves the Active Spot, the engine is slightly too strong in the rare turns where that happens. That reading is unconfirmed and is the only ambiguous point here.

The two small deviations do not push Raticate up:
- The engine offers Roar in Unison as a no-op to an Active Hydreigon under the lock. At most a pilot wastes an Ability.
- Repel cannot target a Fossil. That makes Repel weaker, and no panel deck has Fossils.

So the explanation for the kp3 rise should be looked for in Team Rocket's Raticate ex's Thieving Incisors (the other checker) or in piloting, not in these cards. Nothing was built or run; this was code reading only. votes.reason:
Claim 1 (Binding Snow as a lock on the player) is refuted: the engine does exactly what the card says. Claim 2 (Roar in Unison is offered under the lock) is not refuted: it is a real engine difference, but a tiny one. Neither makes Binding Snow or the Raticate list stronger than the card text, so neither explains the kp3 rise.

Claim 1. The card text (lib/card.py, B2 029) says the lock falls on the opponent and "their Active Pokémon", with no mention of "the Defending Pokémon". It does not depend on Ninetales staying in play.
- The engine stores the lock by turn and applies it to whatever sits in the Active Spot. Only the Energy Zone is blocked, and only for the Active; Bench attaches, discard attaches and energy moves are untouched. It lasts through exactly the opponent's next turn.
- The in-app rule that attack effects end when a Pokémon goes to the Bench is about effects placed on a Pokémon. Cards that mean a Pokémon say so: Stellar Cradle says "the Defending Pokémon", and the engine hangs it on that Pokémon.
- rules/README.md #3 records that effects on the player persist even after the Pokémon that made them is Knocked Out.
- No recording shows Binding Snow or Banette's Night Bind (same text) in play. So Pocket's real behaviour is unconfirmed, but nothing contradicts the engine's reading.

Claim 2. The code confirms it. When Hydreigon is Active under the lock, the engine still offers Roar in Unison. Using it attaches nothing and does no self-damage, but uses up the once-per-turn Ability. The project's rule is that something visibly unable to work is blocked, and the engine follows that rule for Ice Maker. Pocket would most likely grey the Ability out.
- The only cost is a pilot wasting the Ability, then moving Hydreigon to the Bench the same turn, where it could otherwise have used it.
- The same missing check exists for the other self-attach Abilities that don't check the lock (move_generation_abilities.rs 118-119).

votes.reason:
The two claims come out differently. Claim 1 (the Binding Snow lock is on the player) is refuted. Claim 2 (Roar in Unison is offered under the lock) is not refuted, but it is minor and cannot make Binding Snow or the Raticate list stronger than the card text.

CLAIM 1, refuted. The engine does not differ from the card text.
- The text (B2 029, and the same wording on Banette A3 075 Night Bind) is: "During your opponent's next turn, they can't take any Energy from their Energy Zone to attach to their Active Pokémon." The subject is the player, and the object is whatever is their Active. It does not say "the Defending Pokémon".
- Pocket marks effects tied to one Pokémon with that phrase. Gothitelle B1 114 Stellar Cradle says "...to the Defending Pokémon, that Pokémon will be Asleep". The engine keeps that as a CardEffect on the Pokémon (effects.rs 106-108) and keeps Binding Snow as a player-wide TurnEffect. That split matches the two wordings.
- The in-app rule that effects end when a Pokémon goes to the Bench covers effects "on a Pokémon". The project docs say player-wide effects persist even after their source is Knocked Out (rules/04 line 122, observed with Happiny; rules/README 65-66).
- A community source (TheGamer, on Night Bind, same text) says you cannot switch your Active out to escape the lock.
- The rest of the text also checks out. The lock lasts only the opponent's next turn (add_turn_effect with duration 1 covers turn N, which ends with the attack, and turn N+1). It blocks only slot 0 (energy.rs 76-85). Every Zone attach to the Active is blocked: the turn's energy (move_generation/mod.rs 83) and every Ability, attack or Trainer attach that goes through attach_energy_from_zone (energy.rs 21). Benched Pokémon are unaffected, which the text allows. Nothing here does more than the text says.
- The claim's own status was "unclear", and its own reading was that the engine follows the text.

CLAIM 2, not refuted. It is real but has no effect on the Raticate result.
- move_generation_abilities.rs 120 offers AttachEnergyFromZoneToSelfAndDamage (Hydreigon B1 157 Roar in Unison, mapped at effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs 503-508) whenever the Ability is unused. It does not check can_attach_energy_from_zone. Ice Maker's gate at 361-370 does check it.
- apply_common_action_prefix (apply_action_helpers.rs 997-1001) sets ability_used = true before the effect runs. attach_energy_from_zone then returns false (energy.rs 21-23). The 30 self-damage runs only if the attach worked (apply_abilities_action.rs 695-716).
- So an Active Hydreigon under the lock can use up its once-per-turn Ability and get nothing.
- By the project's own rule (RULES_FOR_AGENTS: a play is blocked when what you can see shows it can't work; also the heal-target ruling in rules/04 line 80), Pocket would not offer it. There is no Pocket recording of this case.
- It can only hurt the Hydreigon player: using it, then retreating or switching Hydreigon to the Bench, loses the Bench use of the Ability that turn. It never gives Hydreigon more than the text allows, and never gives Binding Snow more than its text. It cannot explain the Raticate list scoring 57.5% under kp3.

votes.reason:
Claim 1 (Binding Snow as a lock on the player) is REFUTED as an engine-vs-text problem. Claim 2 (Roar in Unison offered as a do-nothing option) is NOT refuted: it is a real but minor move-generation mismatch. The overall verdict is "not refuted" only because of claim 2. Neither claim makes Binding Snow stronger than its text.

Claim 1: the card says "During your opponent's next turn, they can't take any Energy from their Energy Zone to attach to their Active Pokémon." (Alolan Ninetales ex B2 029, [WW] 80, HP 150, Stage 1 from Alolan Vulpix, weak Metal, retreat 2, checked with lib/card.py.) The subject is "they", the player, and the target is "their Active Pokémon", not "the Defending Pokémon". Pocket uses the Pokémon-tied wording when it means the Pokémon hit. Gothitelle B1 114's Stellar Cradle covers the same act, attaching Energy from the Zone, and says "if they attach Energy from their Energy Zone to the Defending Pokémon". The in-app rule "Effects of attacks on a Pokémon end when it goes to the Bench or evolves" covers effects on a Pokémon, so it does not reach a lock worded against the player (like the Item lock, "they can't play any Item cards"). The engine follows the literal text. The only doubt left is how the real game behaves, and no recording shows Binding Snow or Banette's Night Bind, which has identical text. Nothing is found in claims.json, second_pass, rules/ or the Battle Logs.

The engine also does not let Binding Snow do more than the text:
- It blocks only Energy-Zone attaches to slot 0, the Active Spot, and only on the Binding Snow turn and the opponent's next turn.
- Attaching to the Bench, moving Energy between Pokémon, and attaching from the discard pile are not blocked. Those paths use attach_energy_internal or push directly, not attach_energy_from_zone.
- Every Energy-Zone path goes through the check: the turn energy, Abilities, attacks such as Call Forth Cold, Trainers, Misty-style coin flips and Zeraora.

Clemont (B1a 068, text from lib/card.py) says "Put 2 random cards from among Magneton, Heliolisk, and Clemont's Backpack from your deck into your hand." The engine does exactly that. It finds every matching copy in the deck and takes 2 of them (or all of them if there are fewer than 2). Every pair of copies has the same chance, the game's random number generator makes the pick (the player never chooses), and the deck is shuffled afterwards. Picking 2 random cards from the matching cards is the plain reading of the text. Dustin's recording S21 shows one Clemont giving two Backpacks, so two cards with the same name can come together, as they can in the engine. Whether Pocket weights the pick by copy or by name has no source either way (rules/05 #24, filed as low impact). The per-name version is a guess about Pocket's internals, not something the text says, and nothing shows the engine is wrong. With this list's 2 Heliolisk and 2 Backpacks, the engine gives one of each 4/6 of the time and two of the same name 1/6 each. A per-name pick would give one of each 1/2 of the time and a pair 1/4 each. So the most at stake is a small shift in which Clemont results show up. Clemont never gets more cards, other cards, or player-chosen cards, and nothing becomes stronger than its text. At most this is an open question about Pocket, not an engine error.

Ability Thieving Incisors: "Once during your turn, when you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon, you may move a random Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon to this Pokémon." Attack [CC] Boost Dash 70.

- Cyrus: "Switch in 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon that has damage on it to the Active Spot."
- Copycat: "Shuffle your hand into your deck. Draw a card for each card in your opponent's hand."
- Training Area: "Attacks used by Stage 1 Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent's) do +10 damage to the opponent's Active Pokémon."
- Soothing Shore: "At the end of each player's turn, that player heals 20 damage from each of their Pokémon that has any [W] Energy attached."
- Elegant Cape: "The Stage 1 Pokémon this card is attached to gets +30 HP."

MANECTRIC LIST

- Heliolisk (Stage 1): [L] Electrispark 40, "This attack also does 10 damage to each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon."

row.impact_if_wrong:
No card in either list does more against the panel than its text says. I checked Thieving Incisors, Binding Snow, Sabrina, Repel, Cyrus, Copycat, Training Area, Soothing Shore, Elegant Cape, Clemont's Backpack, Electrispark, Thunder Shock, Lightning Accelerator and Field Blower. None of the panel cards that should counter them is weakened either; the one possible slack is minor and works against Hydreigon. The observable parts agree with Dustin's recordings: exactly 1 Energy moved, the ability is optional, the Energy keeps its type, the opponent chooses on Sabrina, Backpacks stack and reach the Bench, and Training Area applies to Stage 1 Pokémon and the Active only.

So the interactions between these lists do not explain Raticate's +16 under kp3 or Manectric's +15 under both pilots. The Raticate lift comes from kp3 actually using a correctly implemented Thieving Incisors, and it is biggest against Vespiquen, Suicune, Weezing, Sceptile, Blaziken and Lucario. That points to piloting: real opponents playing around the steal by attaching to the Bench or holding energy back. It could also be the population, or the Altaria cell's thin real sample (9% on n=32).

Two small deviations do arise in these pairings:
- **Roar in Unison under Binding Snow:** it is offered but does nothing, and it uses up Hydreigon's once-per-turn Ability. Negligible.
